options.text: Period 1 contains eight elements because each period must contain the same number of elements.

Period 1 contains one element because helium is placed outside the periodic table.
Period 1 contains eighteen elements because it includes both s- and p-block elements.

explanation:
Period 1 contains hydrogen and helium only, filling the first shell. Periods 2 and 3 each contain eight elements. Option A incorrectly assumes that all periods have equal lengths.

title: Recognising Dobereiner's triads
question: In Dobereiner's triads, the atomic mass of sodium (23) is approximately the mean of lithium (7) and potassium (39). Which observation best supports this classification?
diagramSvg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 460 180" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#f8fafc; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif;">

      <g transform="translate(60, 45)">
        <rect x="0" y="0" width="90" height="70" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#3b82f6"/>
        <text x="45" y="28" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="800" fill="#1e40af">Lithium (Li)</text>
        <text x="45" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Mass = 7</text>
        
        <rect x="125" y="0" width="90" height="70" rx="6" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#f59e0b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <text x="170" y="28" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="800" fill="#92400e">Sodium (Na)</text>

        <text x="295" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Mass = 39</text>
      </g>
      <!-- Formula -->
      <rect x="100" y="125" width="260" height="34" rx="4" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1"/>
      <text x="230" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">Mean Mass = (7 + 39) / 2 = 23 (Exact match!)</text>

options.text: Their atomic numbers are in the ratio 1:2:3.
All three elements have identical atomic radii and identical reactivity.
The atomic mass of sodium is approximately the arithmetic mean of those of lithium and potassium, and the three elements have similar chemical properties.
Sodium has the same atomic mass as lithium plus potassium.

explanation:
The mean of the outer atomic masses is (7+39)/2=23, approximately sodium's atomic mass. The three alkali metals also share similar chemical properties. Option D incorrectly adds the masses instead of taking their average.

options.text: Mendeleev used electron configurations as the primary basis for arrangement
Mendeleev arranged elements primarily by atomic mass, while the modern table is arranged by atomic number
Mendeleev's table contained exactly 18 groups
The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing neutron number

explanation:
Mendeleev used increasing atomic mass while prioritizing similarities in chemical properties. The modern periodic table uses increasing atomic number, which resolves several anomalies in the earlier arrangement.

**Tempting distractor:** Option C incorrectly applies the modern table's 18-group structure to Mendeleev's original arrangement.

title: An element forms a stable 2+ ion and its oxide has the formula XO. Which conclusion is most justified?
question: An element forms a stable 2+ ion and its oxide has the formula XO. Which conclusion is most justified?

options.text: X must be a noble gas
X must be a Group 17 element
X can be a Group 2 element, although the formula alone does not establish its exact identity
X must have seven valence electrons

explanation:
In XO, oxygen typically has oxidation state -2. Electrical neutrality therefore requires X to have oxidation state +2. Group 2 elements commonly form 2+ ions, so this is consistent with the evidence, but it does not uniquely identify the element.

**Tempting distractor:** Option D describes the usual valence-electron count of Group 17 elements, which generally form 1- ions rather than 2+ ions.

title: Board-style Isotopes and periodic position
question: Two isotopes of chlorine have mass numbers 35 and 37. Which statement is correct?

options.text: They occupy the same position in the modern periodic table because they have the same atomic number
They occupy different groups because their neutron counts differ
The isotope with mass number 37 must be in a lower period
The isotope with mass number 35 has one more proton

explanation:
Both isotopes have 17 protons and therefore atomic number 17. They differ in neutron count, not proton count, so they have the same periodic position and broadly similar chemical properties.

title: Board-style Recognising blocks
question: An element has the outer electronic configuration 3s² 3p⁴. Which conclusion is correct?

title: Board-style Periodic trends and effective nuclear attraction
question: Two elements P and Q are in the same period, with Q positioned to the right of P. Which statement is generally expected?

title: Board-style Comparing metallic and nonmetallic behaviour
question: Consider sodium, magnesium, silicon and chlorine in Period 3. Which statement best describes the broad trend?

options.text: Metallic character generally decreases from sodium toward chlorine
Metallic character increases continuously from sodium to chlorine
All four elements have the same metallic character
Chlorine is the most metallic because it has the most valence electrons

title: Board-style Choosing the correct explanation
question: An element has a relatively large atomic radius and low first ionisation energy compared with another element in the same period. Which explanation is most consistent with these properties?

options.text: It has a higher effective nuclear attraction for its valence electrons
It has a smaller outermost shell radius
Its valence electrons are more strongly held by the nucleus
Its valence electrons experience weaker effective attraction and are more easily removed

explanation:
A larger atomic radius and lower first ionisation energy are generally associated with valence electrons that are less strongly attracted to the nucleus. Such electrons are easier to remove.

**Tempting distractor:** Option A predicts stronger attraction, which would generally favour a smaller atom and a higher ionisation energy.

title: Board-style Interpreting successive ionisation energies
question: An element has a very large jump between its second and third ionisation energies. Which conclusion is most likely?

options.text: It has seven valence electrons
It belongs to Group 17
It is a noble gas
It has two valence electrons, and removing the third electron would disrupt a stable inner shell

explanation:
The first two electrons can be removed from the outer shell. After those are removed, the third electron must come from a more stable inner shell, requiring much more energy. This pattern is characteristic of an element with two valence electrons, such as magnesium.

**Tempting distractor:** Option B suggests seven valence electrons, for which the largest jump would normally occur after removal of the seventh electron.

question: Which pair correctly illustrates an exception to the simple rule that first ionisation energy increases continuously across a period?
